kinds.a: wheelchair ramp · threshold ramp · suitcase ramp
kinds.d: Movable ramp that lets a wheelchair or scooter cross steps, kerbs or door thresholds.

kinds.a: hoist · Hoyer lift · sling lift · stand aid
kinds.d: Powered or hydraulic hoist that lifts a person in a sling or standing frame between bed, chair and toilet.

kinds.a: transfer board · sliding board · turntable · pivot disc · standing aid
kinds.d: Non-powered aid that helps a person slide, pivot or stand to move between bed, chair, car and wheelchair.

kinds.a: scooter lift · boot hoist · hitch lift
kinds.d: Powered lift fitted inside a car or on its hitch that raises a mobility scooter or wheelchair into or onto the vehicle.

notes: Shelf rebuilt as 4 tier kinds (3 carried over plus new "Transfer aid"). Portable ramp: kept the market-covering ramp models, dropped EZ-ACCESS TRAVERSE (a walk/storage ramp, not really for wheelchair access) and moved ramp styles into t. Patient lift: grew from 3 Invacare-only models to 10 across Joerns (Hoyer/Oxford), Invacare, Etac (Molift) and Arjo, as the brief asked. Arjo Maxi Move and Sara Flex are mostly used in care homes, but they stay because Arjo was named. Ceiling-track hoists are left out as a type because they are built in, so they belong in G3 Home Fixtures. The stairlift was not in this shelf's old data and goes to G3 under the rules, so there is nothing to move here and no moves file entry. Transfer aid (new): its source is the Wikipedia article on transfer boards. Its models are Arjo Sara Stedy, Etac Turner Pro, Performance Health MediDisk and the Autochair Transfer Plate. Mobility vehicle lift: the old source (the scooterdirect.com homepage) is replaced by Bruno's lift page, which I retrieved. Models are from Bruno, Harmar and Autochair. Brand register: country and founding year are left blank where no page I retrieved stated them (Joerns, Harmar, plus founding years for Bruno, EZ-ACCESS and Autochair). I gave no brand entries to the small ramp makers (National Ramp, Prairie View Industries, Roll-A-Ramp, Stepless) or to Performance Health because I retrieved no brand page for them. I didn't fetch Which?, CHOICE or Consumer Reports test-winner sources for this shelf. The Wikipedia tool failed (lock error), so all sources come from web_fetch. This is a tier shelf, so there are no archetypes.
